summary: The study focuses on optimizing Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) of HfO2 for sub-1 nm equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) in advanced semiconductor devices. The process uses HfCl4 and H2O as precursors, with optimization of parameters such as H2O pulse time, deposition temperature, and intermediate treatments like plasma or cooling to enhance growth-per-cycle (GPC) and reduce Cl impurities. The results show that saturated H2O pulses (10 s) improve electrical properties by reducing gate leakage current and achieving lower EOT.
evidence: The implementation of HfO2 gate dielectrics in sub-45 nm devices requires optimization of nanometer-thin HfO2 layers, deposited, e.g., by atomic layer deposition. In this work, we optimize ALD conditions such as precursor pulse time and deposition temperature for HfO2 layers with physical thicknesses below 2 nm. Additionally, we investigate intermediate treatments in the ALD reaction cycle, such as exposure to gas-phase moisture or remote plasma at low temperature and thermal anneals. Such intermediate treatments affect both growth-per-cycle and Cl-impurity content of the HfO2 layers. The analysis of the process modifications allows a better understanding of the reaction mechanisms. H2O pulse times of 10 s must be applied to achieve saturation in GPC and Cl content. Using saturated H2O pulses decreases the gate leakage current in the sub-1 nm equivalent oxide thickness range. The GPC is enhanced from 1.8 Hf/nm2 for conventional ALD to 4 Hf/nm2 for intermediate plasma treatments at low temperature. Intermediate anneals reduce the Cl content by about two orders of magnitude.
